specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** scribe-or-press
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** calculate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will calculate the number of copies at which printing a 200-page book becomes cheaper than copying it by hand, for an ordinary copyist and for a master calligrapher, predicting each crossover within one copy. **Prerequisites:** scribe, copyist, movable type, printing press, fixed cost, marginal cost (defined in the sections "Scribes and Copyists", "Gutenberg" and "The Printing Press" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each scribe type, the learner enters a predicted crossover number of copies before moving the slider to check it. A prediction is correct if it is within 1 of the true crossover in Rules (15 for the ordinary copyist, 4 for the master calligrapher). Mastery is both predictions correct within two attempts each. **Misconceptions:** (1) The press was cheaper for every job, even a single copy. (2) The press's advantage was only speed, not cost per copy. (3) Making books more beautiful by hand always made them better value. (4) The cost of a press is mostly in running it, rather than in setting it up. **Instructional Rationale:** Calculating the crossover requires the learner to apply the fixed-cost and marginal-cost model to numbers, and comparing two scribe types shows how the crossover moves when hand-copying gets slower. Predicting before checking turns the slider into a test of the model rather than a toy. **Content:** All costs are in workdays, one person's day of skilled work. The book has 200 pages. The sim labels all numbers "Illustrative model, not historical prices." | Method | Rate | Fixed cost | Cost per copy | |---|---|---|---| | Ordinary copyist | 8 pages per day | 0 | 200 ÷ 8 = 25 workdays | | Master calligrapher | 2 pages per day | 0 | 200 ÷ 2 = 100 workdays | | Printing press | Casting type, building the press, and setting 200 pages | 350 workdays | 0.2 workdays (printing, paper handling, binding labor) | **Provenance:** Illustrative model written for this chapter. The rates are round numbers chosen to show the shape of the comparison, consistent with the chapter's description of slow hand-copying (section "Scribes and Copyists") and Gutenberg's high setup cost (section "Gutenberg"); they are not historical prices. **Rules:** - Copies slider: min 1, max 500, step 1, default 1, unit copies. - Scribe type selector: "Ordinary copyist" (default) or "Master calligrapher". - Scribe cost = copies × (200 ÷ pages per day). Press cost = 350 + 0.2 × copies. - The crossover is the smallest whole number of copies for which press cost < scribe cost. Ordinary copyist: 25 × N > 350 + 0.2 × N gives N > 14.1, so the crossover is 15 copies. Master calligrapher: 100 × N > 350 + 0.2 × N gives N > 3.51, so the crossover is 4 copies. - At the current slider value, the sim shows both costs in workdays, rounded to one decimal place, and states which method is cheaper; at equal cost (which does not occur at whole copy numbers with these values) it would state "equal". - Reference values at default and at 200 copies: 1 copy, ordinary copyist 25.0 vs press 350.2; 200 copies, ordinary copyist 5,000.0 vs press 390.0. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the three methods and their costs. 2. With "Ordinary copyist" selected, the learner types a predicted crossover and presses Check Prediction. 3. The learner moves the copies slider and watches both cost lines; the sim marks the crossover. 4. The learner switches to "Master calligrapher", predicts again, and checks. 5. The learner moves the slider to 200 copies and compares the two costs. 6. The learner should notice that the slower and more beautiful the handwriting, the sooner the press wins. **Feedback:** After each prediction: within 1 of the true crossover shows "Correct: from [true crossover] copies, the press is cheaper." Otherwise, "Not quite. Try setting scribe cost equal to press cost: [scribe cost per copy] × N = 350 + 0.2 × N." A learner gets two attempts per scribe type; after the second miss the sim reveals the crossover with the worked equation from Rules. When both scribe types are done, the sim shows "The press costs more to start and less to copy. That is why it won for any book wanted by more than a handful of readers." **Starting State:** Copies set to 1, "Ordinary copyist" selected, both costs shown (25.0 vs 350.2 workdays, scribe cheaper), and the question "How many copies before the press is cheaper?" **Chapter Anchors:** 200-page book; ordinary copyist 8 pages a day; master calligrapher 2 pages a day; press fixed cost 350 workdays and 0.2 per copy; crossovers at 15 and 4 copies; illustrative numbers.
